newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Closing Australian stocks feel weight of big banks.
newsitem.headline: Closing Australian stocks feel weight of big banks.

text.p: SPI Futures 2533 -4 US 30yr cl 6.88 -0.05
10yrbond futs 92.300 +0.090 Gold NY 347.05 Lon fix 349.10
*Stocks fall in choppy trade, banks feature as NAB reports half year and leads market down. Volume 296.25 million, value A$790.08 million, 1,087 stocks traded, 346 steady, 332 up, 409 down.
A patchy Australian share market closed slightly lower on Thursday, weighed down by a volatile bank sector.
The All Ordinaries index lost 5.4 points to 2,525.0.
June share price index futures were down four points at 2,533, an eight point premium to the underlying index.

Bank sector leader National Australia Bank posted a 14.1 percent jump in first half net profit to A$1.14 billion, but warned that margins were down across the board, confirming a similarly downbeat forecast made on Wednesday by rival big four bank, Westpac Banking Corp.

NAB shares headed sharply lower after the midday result, touching an intraday low of A$17.99 barely two hours after they had touched a record high A$18.55. They regained some ground to end 23 cents lower at A$18.13.
"It looks like it will be a bit harder for the banks in the future," said a senior dealer at a Brisbane-based brokerage firm.
But he noted that recent rises in the sector, and in NAB in particular, had been dramatic.
"They have had an incredible run with NAB even reaching A$18.55 this morning at one stage."
In the last month alone, NAB shares have rocketed 17 percent to this morning's record high A$18.55 from A$15.88 on April 15.

The three remaining big banks also ended lower. ANZ Bank, which issuues its half year report next week, fell 3.7 cents to A$8.43 while Commonwealth Bank of Australia ended 13 cents lower at AS14.63 after Wednesday's record high of A$14.72. Westpac shed 12 cents to A$7.321.

Among others, Rupert Murdoch's media giant News Corp saw active trade with 8.1 million shares dealt. It ended down two at A$5.70 after going as low as A$5.63 amid fears the acquisitive mogul was about to spend up big yet again.
"The market is really worried where the money is going to come from," the Brisbane-based dealer said.

Newcrest Mining continued to rise, ending 10 cents higher at A$3.56 in response to Wednesday's abrupt departure of managing director John Quinn. The company is now looking at ways to save its struggling Telfer gold mine.
Advertising group Singleton Group ended up 50 cents at A$6.60 after it announced a 23 cents per share capital return in addition to its special dividend of A$1.70 per share.
Falls shaded rises just by a ratio of about six to five, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active with similar choppy trade as the underlying market. Options trade was modest.
Total options traded 31,425 (21,592)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 7,060 (7,601)

In other local markets, Australian debt futures closed sharply higher as the market once again got fidgety over the domestic monetary policy outlook, brushing aside the post-budget disappointment that has overhung the market since Tuesday.
By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.68 percent, down from Tuesday's 7.77 percent.
The Australian dollar spent much of Thursday submerged beneath a wave of offshore selling, but did get a late lifeline on domestic rates which at least kept it afloat against the U.S. dollar.
By 5.10 p.m., sufficient support had been found to push the local dollar to US$0.7763/68 from US$0.7782/87 late here Wednesday.
